node.label: Other sports
node.summary: Noteworthy results in sports without a dedicated branch (kabaddi, motorsport, boxing, etc.).

facts.text: **Manav Thakkar** won his first international singles title at **WTT Feeder Chennai**, beating England's Samuel Walker in the final; **Sutirtha Mukherjee** was runner-up in women's singles to Korea's Yoo Yerin.
facts.plain: Manav Thakkar won his first international singles title at WTT Feeder Chennai, beating England's Samuel Walker in the final; Sutirtha Mukherjee was runner-up in women's singles to Korea's Yoo Yerin.

facts.text: **Marc Marquez** moved to the brink of an eighth MotoGP world title after winning the Malaysian GP, extending his points lead to 399 (second-placed brother Alex Marquez on 355) with three race weekends left.
facts.plain: Marc Marquez moved to the brink of an eighth MotoGP world title after winning the Malaysian GP, extending his points lead to 399 (second-placed brother Alex Marquez on 355) with three race weekends left.

facts.text: India's men's and women's kabaddi teams won the titles at the inaugural **Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship** in Ahmedabad; the men beat Sri Lanka 54-20 and the women beat Uganda 35-15.
facts.plain: India's men's and women's kabaddi teams won the titles at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in Ahmedabad; the men beat Sri Lanka 54-20 and the women beat Uganda 35-15.

facts.text: Dakar 2026 is the first Olympic event of any kind held in **Africa**; the Youth Olympic Games began in **2010** (Singapore).
facts.plain: Dakar 2026 is the first Olympic event of any kind held in Africa; the Youth Olympic Games began in 2010 (Singapore).

facts.text: **P.B. Abhinandh** upset fourth seed Kwon Hyuk at **WTT Feeder Chennai**; Senegal-born **Ibrahima Diaw** (two Olympics for Senegal) now plays WTT events for Denmark.
facts.plain: P.B. Abhinandh upset fourth seed Kwon Hyuk at WTT Feeder Chennai; Senegal-born Ibrahima Diaw (two Olympics for Senegal) now plays WTT events for Denmark.

facts.text: **Neeraj Chopra** (two-time Olympic medallist) missed the **Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games** (Japan) with an ankle injury and will resume training soon.
facts.plain: Neeraj Chopra (two-time Olympic medallist) missed the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games (Japan) with an ankle injury and will resume training soon.

facts.text: India finished **87th of 189** at the inaugural **FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival** in **Baku**.
facts.plain: India finished 87th of 189 at the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku.

facts.text: **Senegal** hosts the **Youth Olympic Games** in **Dakar** (31 Oct-13 Nov 2026).
facts.plain: Senegal hosts the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar (31 Oct-13 Nov 2026).

facts.text: Indian women's best-ever Worlds: gold (Manisha Bhanwala, 59kg), silver (**Neelam Sirohi** 50kg, **Kajal Dhochak** 76kg), bronze (**Tanu Sharma** 72kg); India finished 4th in the women's section.
facts.plain: Indian women's best-ever Worlds: gold (Manisha Bhanwala, 59kg), silver (Neelam Sirohi 50kg, Kajal Dhochak 76kg), bronze (Tanu Sharma 72kg); India finished 4th in the women's section.

facts.text: **Manisha Bhanwala** (Haryana) won **59kg gold** at the **World Wrestling Championships** in **Astana**, beating USA's Abigail Nette 8-6 — the **first Indian woman** to win a world title and India's second world champion after **Sushil Kumar** (66kg, Moscow 2010).
facts.plain: Manisha Bhanwala (Haryana) won 59kg gold at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana, beating USA's Abigail Nette 8-6 — the first Indian woman to win a world title and India's second world champion after Sushil Kumar (66kg, Moscow 2010).

facts.text: Japan's **Daiki Hashimoto** won a **fourth straight all-around title** at the Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in **Rotterdam** (his 7th world gold). The Worlds began in **1903** (Antwerp); women's events from **1934**.
facts.plain: Japan's Daiki Hashimoto won a fourth straight all-around title at the Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in Rotterdam (his 7th world gold). The Worlds began in 1903 (Antwerp); women's events from 1934.

facts.text: World Wrestling Championships (**Astana**): **Manisha Bhanwala** (59kg) reached the final; **Neelam Sirohi** (50kg) and **Kajal Dhochak** (76kg) won silver.
facts.plain: World Wrestling Championships (Astana): Manisha Bhanwala (59kg) reached the final; Neelam Sirohi (50kg) and Kajal Dhochak (76kg) won silver.

facts.text: **WTT Feeder Chennai** is held at the Tamil Nadu Physical Education and Sports University; **Ankur Bhattacharjee** (19, reigning Commonwealth champion) was seeded 2nd behind **Manav Thakkar**.
facts.plain: WTT Feeder Chennai is held at the Tamil Nadu Physical Education and Sports University; Ankur Bhattacharjee (19, reigning Commonwealth champion) was seeded 2nd behind Manav Thakkar.

facts.text: **Mirabai Chanu** withdrew from the women's 53kg event at the **World Weightlifting Championships** in **Ningbo** (China) with a back sprain.
facts.plain: Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the women's 53kg event at the World Weightlifting Championships in Ningbo (China) with a back sprain.
